orchestrator.title: Orchestrator
orchestrator.manageContextUnavailable: Choosing what each reply gets isn't built yet: each reply gets the Orchestrator's rules and this conversation.

start.title: What should we plan?
start.description: Discuss an idea, break work into tasks, check on the queue or ask how things are going. A task the Orchestrator creates stays a draft until a run starts.

composer.placeholderNew: Describe what you want to build, or ask about this project…
composer.permissionsHint: Every action it takes is checked like the same action in the app, with your permissions in this project.
composer.notReady: Choose and publish what the Orchestrator runs on in its settings first.
composer.thinking: The Orchestrator answers one message at a time.

context.line: Each reply gets the Orchestrator's rules and this conversation

suggestions.plan: Plan work from a scope file: tasks with briefs and acceptance criteria.
suggestions.running: What's running, what's waiting and what's blocked right now?
suggestions.order: Suggest an order for the Todo tasks and which can run in parallel.
suggestions.idea: Talk through an idea before it becomes a task.
suggestions.note: A suggestion fills the prompt so you can edit it. Nothing is sent until you press Send.

orchestrator.footer: Conversations stay in History for {{project}} · each task keeps its own Conversation
orchestrator.stopNote: Stop response ends this answer only. Tasks, runs and the queue are not touched.

stopped.nothing: Response stopped by you · {{time}} · nothing was created or changed
stopped.acted: Response stopped by you · {{time}} · what it did before stays

orchestrator.interrupted: The answer was cut short when Orchester or its runner closed
orchestrator.askAgainNote: Sends your last message once more.

failure.notSignedIn: The connection's CLI isn't signed in on this computer. Your message and this conversation are kept; nothing else changed.
failure.cannotStart: The connection's CLI couldn't be started; the runner's log says why. Your message and this conversation are kept; nothing else changed.
failure.connectionGone: The Orchestrator's connection is gone or can't run it. Choose another in Orchestrator settings; this conversation is kept.
failure.accountNone: The connection has no account to sign in with; choose one in Connections. Your message and this conversation are kept.
failure.accountFolderMissing: The account's folder {{folder}} is gone; choose another account in Connections. Your message and this conversation are kept.
failure.accountUnsupported: This connection's account can't be used on this computer yet; choose Default in Connections. Your message and this conversation are kept.
failure.failedBody: {{reason}} · Your message and this conversation are kept.
failure.earlierNotSignedIn: This answer failed: the CLI wasn't signed in
failure.earlierUnreachable: This answer failed: the Orchestrator couldn't start
failure.timeLimit: It ran longer than {{minutes}} minutes, the most one answer may take, and was ended. What it did until then stays; ask again in smaller parts.
failure.earlierTimeLimit: This answer was ended after {{minutes}} minutes

sendProblem.body: Your draft is kept. Retry sends it once; it is never stored twice.

orchestrator.setupFailed: What the Orchestrator runs on couldn't be read

notReady.title: Choose what the Orchestrator runs on
notReady.body: Pick a Claude Code connection and a model in Orchestrator settings and publish them. Conversations stay readable; new messages can't be sent until then.

loading.title: Loading conversation…
loading.note: Messages load together. Suggestions don't show while loading.

notFound.title: This conversation isn't in {{project}}
notFound.body: It may have been removed with its project data. Start a new conversation or open one from History.

createTask.effect: It is in Tasks as a draft. Nothing is queued and no agent has started.

updateTask.effect: Its details changed as Edit task changes them.

runTask.effect: It runs as Start in Tasks runs it, after the queue's checks.

pauseRun.effect: The run pauses at its agents' next checkpoint.

resumeRun.effect: The run goes on from where it stopped.

holdQueue.effect: Running runs go on; queued tasks wait until you release them in Tasks.

releaseQueue.effect: Queued tasks start again as their groups allow.

duplicatePipeline.done: Copied a pipeline as a draft
duplicatePipeline.effect: The copy is a draft: no task runs it until its first version is published.

action.checked: Checked like the same action in the app, with your permissions in {{project}}.

newSession.connection: The Orchestrator runs on another connection now: this answer starts a new session and doesn't remember the earlier messages.
newSession.account: The Orchestrator's connection is on another account now: this answer starts a new session and doesn't remember the earlier messages.

held.projectEffect: No waiting task in {{project}} starts until you resume. Running tasks keep running.
held.groupTitle: New starts held · the group of {{task}}
held.groupEffect: No waiting task in this group starts until you resume. Running tasks keep running.
held.checked: Same action as Pause scheduling in the queue, checked against your permissions in {{project}}.

proposal.title: Start {{task}} on {{pipeline}}?
proposal.effect: Nothing has started. The Orchestrator asked to start this run; it starts only when you choose Start, after the queue's checks.
proposal.briefCut: This is only the opening of the brief: open {{task}} to read all of it before you start.
proposal.personOnly: Only a person starts a run the Orchestrator proposed: input from automation is refused here.

historyPanel.title: History
historyPanel.empty: No conversation yet. Your first message starts one.
historyPanel.noMatch: No conversation's title has these words.
historyPanel.note: Only conversations in {{project}}. Opening one keeps your draft; Esc closes History.

settings.description: Plans work with you, drafts tasks and coordinates {{project}}'s queue.

publish.firstNote: The project chat can send once v1 is published.
publish.needsConnection: Publishing needs a connection that can run the Orchestrator.
publish.needsModel: Publishing needs a model: choose one, or type an id the connection accepts.

tabs.notBuilt: These settings aren't built yet: the Orchestrator acts with the project's permissions, reads the repository and keeps every conversation.

connection.label: Project connection
connection.description: The agent CLI and sign-in the Orchestrator runs on.

model.label: Model
model.description: From the connection's list, or Other model id… for one that isn't listed.
model.otherHint: Enter an id the connection accepts
model.invalid: A model id has no spaces and is at most {{max}} characters long.

effort.label: Reasoning effort
effort.description: CLI default leaves it to the connection's own setting.
effort.unchecked: Not checked for this model: the connection lists no efforts for it, so these are its other models'.

settings.note: A reply already under way finishes on the version it started with; a published change applies from the next reply.
settings.limits: Its tokens count toward {{project}}'s daily budget; it takes no agent slot. One answer ends after {{turns}} steps or {{minutes}} minutes.

noConnection.title: No connection in {{project}} can run the Orchestrator
noConnection.body: It needs an agent connection that answers and is signed in. Conversations stay readable; new messages can't be sent until one works.

personOnly.publish: Only a person publishes a draft the Orchestrator proposed: input from automation is refused here.
personOnly.cancel: Only a person cancels a run the Orchestrator proposed: input from automation is refused here.
personOnly.merge: Only a person merges a run the Orchestrator proposed: input from automation is refused here.

publish.effectWaits: Nothing is published yet. Agents read v{{before}} until you publish v{{version}}; a run already under way keeps the version it started with.
publish.effectWaitsProfile: Nothing is published yet. {{name}} keeps v{{before}} until you publish v{{version}}.
publish.effectFirst: Nothing is published yet. No agent gets {{name}} until you publish v{{version}}.
publish.effectApplied: Agents read v{{version}} from their next step.
publish.effectAppliedKeeping: Agents read v{{version}} from their next step. The {{count}} runs under way keep v{{before}} until they finish.
publish.effectAppliedKeepingOne: Agents read v{{version}} from their next step. The run under way keeps v{{before}} until it finishes.
publish.effectDone: Let the Orchestrator publish drafts is on, so the chat published it without asking. Agents read v{{version}} from their next step.
publish.effectDoneKeeping: Let the Orchestrator publish drafts is on, so the chat published it without asking. Agents read v{{version}} from their next step; runs under way keep v{{before}}.
publish.effectDismissed: You dismissed it. Nothing was published; the draft stays in {{place}}.
publish.widens: This draft widens what {{name}} may do, so it waits for you even though Let the Orchestrator publish drafts is on. Let automation change agent permissions is off.
publish.publishedAs: Published as Publish in {{place}} publishes it, with your permissions in {{project}}.

cancel.effectWaits: Nothing has stopped yet. Cancel stops the run's agents now; its worktree, branch and finished steps stay so you can read what it did. Nothing is merged or deleted.
cancel.effectApplied: Its agents stopped at {{time}}. The worktree and the branch {{branch}} are kept; {{task}} can run again from Tasks.
cancel.effectAppliedPlain: Its agents stopped at {{time}}. Its worktree and branch are kept; {{task}} can run again from Tasks.
cancel.effectDismissed: You dismissed it. The run goes on.

merge.effectWaitsInto: Nothing is merged yet. Merge into {{into}} merges it as Merge in the task's review does, after the same checks.
merge.effectWaits: Nothing is merged yet. Merge merges it as Merge in the task's review does, after the same checks.
merge.effectDismissed: You dismissed it. Nothing was merged; the run stays ready for review.

start.effect: Auto mode is on in {{project}}, so the Orchestrator started this run without asking. It went through the queue's checks, as Start in Tasks does.

facts.diffCut: More of the text changes: open the draft to read all of it.
facts.unreadable: What this card acts on can't be read: {{reason}}

widens.writableFolder: a writable folder outside the worktree
widens.stepToolCalls: step {{step}} tool calls not asked about
